THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  127

[Photograph and handwritten letter reproduced as photostat]

SAVOY COLLEGE

My father attending Savoy College of importance was a very happy one.

To begin with it, was not the school of my choosing[?], but that of my fathers[?], after having attended the school for some months I knew that it was the school of my choice also.

The fact that I was so father did take place in a class by himself[?], this situation was truly appreciated by all fellow students.

By mixing and mingling with those who had a greater portion of education than I did at father. however we were afforded an opportunity to have spent a number of situations with a broader view point than if we had been able to continue[?] ourselves and our associates. This condition of life which taught[?] me an association of equals[?].

Because of the impressive spirit prevailing in Savoy College[?] it leaves a fine friend to the Indians[?], no matter what degree of attainment or importance while attending this school, was a very pleasant and satisfactory one.

[Signed] James[?] [illegible]
[illegible] Rutherford[?]
[illegible] at
[illegible] [?]
notes: Page 127 of printed text. This page contains a reproduced photostat of a handwritten letter. The handwriting is difficult to read and portions are marked as illegible or uncertain.
